intro: Nepal, home of Mount Everest and the birthplace of the Buddha, was never colonised and became a republic in 2008.

chapters.title: Birthplace of the Buddha
text: Siddhartha Gautama, who became the Buddha, was born at Lumbini in southern Nepal around 2,500 years ago. The Indian emperor Ashoka later put up a stone pillar there.
The Kathmandu Valley was ruled by the Licchavi and then the Malla kings, whose cities of Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur are full of temples, palaces and carved wooden windows.

chapters.title: Unification
text: In 1768 Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha conquered the valley and founded the Shah dynasty, uniting Nepal. A war with the British East India Company in 1814 to 1816 cost Nepal land but left it independent.
Gurkha soldiers from Nepal have served in the British Army ever since.

highlight.title: Gurkhas
highlight.text: Gurkha regiments, known for the curved khukuri knife, have served Britain for over 200 years.

chapters.title: Ranas, kings and a republic
text: From 1846 to 1951 the Rana family ruled as hereditary prime ministers. Democracy came and went under the kings. A Maoist insurgency from 1996 to 2006 killed about 17,000 people, and in 2001 Crown Prince Dipendra killed much of the royal family.
In 2008 Nepal abolished the monarchy and became a republic. A huge earthquake in 2015 killed about 9,000 people. In September 2025 youth-led protests toppled the government.

keyTerms.meaning: Nepali soldiers serving in the British and Indian armies.
A country with an elected head of state instead of a monarch.
